GLOSSARY
1G: First generation wireless cellular technology that offered basic voice calls, had speeds up to
2.4 Kbps, and used an analog signal.
2G: Second generation wireless cellular technology that offered improved quality and capacity, had speeds up to 64
Kbps, and used digital signals. 2G was the first system that allowed for text and picture messages.
3G: Third generation wireless cellular technology that increased speeds up to 2 Mbps, uses digital broadband, and
brought the first wave of smart phones that allowed for faster communication, larger emails/texts, fast web
browsing, and video streaming.
4G: The current wireless communication system, with higher speeds starting at 100 Mbps, a mandated use of IP, and
a simplified 3G network, reducing transfer latency and increasing the speed and efficiency of the network.
5G: Fifth-generation wireless cellular technology that will have speeds at a minimum of 1Gbps as compared to a
minimum of 100 Mbps with 4G. It will support higher speeds, capacity, faster data transmission, and better multi-
media clarity than the previous generation.
AV: Autonomous Vehicles that can guide themselves without human control.
CDMA: Code-Division Multiple Access, a channel access method used by numerous radio communication
technologies. Using CDMA, a transmitter can send information simultaneously over a single communication channel.
CV: Connected Vehicles refer to the presence of devices in the car that can connect with other devices in the car, or
devices, networks, or services outside of the car, including other cars or infrastructure.
DSL: Digital Subscriber Line, the way in which a computer connects to the internet at high speeds using phone lines.
EDGE: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution, is a digital phone technology that allows for
higher data transmission rates.
EV: Electric Vehicles that use electric motors instead of gasoline for fuel. Electric Vehicles have rechargeable batteries
that power the motor.
Fiber-Optic: Glass or plastic threads used to transmit light signals holding data with little to no loss of strength.
Gbps: Billions of bits per second, the measure of bandwidth on a digital data transmission, such as fiber.
GSM: Global Systems for Mobile Communication, a digital mobile network used by phones.
Kbps: Thousands of bits or kilobits per second, a measure of bandwidth on a digital data transmission, such as fiber.
ICT: Information and Communications Technology, the technology that supports different types of information or
communications systems or devices.
IMT: Advanced - International Mobile Telecommunications-Advanced, a standard system created by the International
Telecommunication Union for the creation, operation, and management of next generation mobile networks.
IP: Internet Protocol, a set of rules that dictate the format of data sent over the internet or any other network.
Macrocell: Traditional cell towers that provide coverage for several miles.
Mbps: Millions of bits or megabits per second, a measure of bandwidth on a digital data transmission, such as fiber.
P3: Public-Private-Partnerships, the partnership between a government (public) body and a private partner to
produce projects using private money that can provide a public good.
